title: Grid over-voltage
symptoms: Inverter trips or derates during the day; display shows grid voltage high (often >253 V single phase or >440 V three phase). Common at midday in areas with many rooftop systems or at the end of long LT lines.
causes: Utility/DISCOM grid voltage genuinely above inverter limit
Undersized or long AC cable causing voltage rise at inverter terminals
Loose AC terminal raising local voltage
Grid code / country setting configured too strict
steps: Measure AC voltage at inverter terminals and at the main distribution board with a multimeter while the inverter is producing
If voltage at the board is already high, log readings and raise a complaint with the DISCOM
Check AC cable size and length against design; voltage drop should be under 1-2%
Tighten AC terminals with power isolated (AC breaker OFF, DC isolator OFF)
Verify the inverter grid code is set to the correct country/state standard (e.g. India CEA)

title: Grid under-voltage
symptoms: Inverter disconnects in the evening or during peak load hours; display shows grid voltage low (often <180-195 V).
causes: Weak grid / heavy local load at evening peak
Faulty AC breaker or MCB with high contact resistance
Wrong phase wiring on three-phase inverter
steps: Measure voltage at inverter AC terminals and at the meter
Check neutral connection at the inverter, ACDB and meter for looseness or heating marks
Inspect AC MCB/RCCB for burn marks; replace if contact resistance is high
If grid is genuinely low, register a DISCOM complaint; inverter auto-reconnects when voltage recovers

title: Grid over-frequency
symptoms: Inverter reports grid frequency above limit (e.g. >50.5 Hz) and disconnects briefly.
causes: Running on a diesel generator with poor governor
steps: Check whether the site was on DG backup at the time of the fault
Read fault log timestamps; isolated short events are usually grid-side and self-clearing
Confirm frequency protection settings match the local grid code
Never connect a grid-tie inverter to a DG without a proper DG-sync controller

title: Grid under-frequency
symptoms: Inverter reports grid frequency below limit (e.g. <49.5 Hz) and disconnects.
causes: Utility frequency dip during heavy load
Incorrect frequency settings (60 Hz profile on a 50 Hz grid)
steps: Verify the inverter is set to 50 Hz grid profile
Check if fault coincides with DG operation
If frequent and grid-side, monitor and inform DISCOM; inverter reconnects automatically

title: No grid / grid loss (anti-islanding)
symptoms: Inverter shows no grid and produces nothing even in sunlight.
steps: Confirm whether there is a power cut in the area
Check the AC MCB and RCCB in the ACDB are ON; reset once if tripped
If RCCB trips repeatedly, treat as earth leakage fault and do not keep resetting
Inspect AC connector at the inverter for burn marks with power isolated

title: Isolation / insulation resistance fault (Riso low)
symptoms: Inverter refuses to start in the morning or after rain; shows insulation resistance low. Often clears as the day dries out.
causes: Damaged DC cable insulation (rodent bites, sharp edges, UV)
Water ingress in MC4 connectors or junction boxes
Cracked panel backsheet or damaged module junction box
Wet DC cables lying in water on the roof
steps: Isolate the DC side (DC isolator OFF) and wear insulated gloves; PV strings remain live in daylight
Disconnect strings one at a time at the inverter to find which string triggers the fault
Use an insulation tester (1000 V megger) on the suspect string, positive and negative to earth; expect >1 MOhm
Inspect MC4 connectors for moisture and replace any with water or corrosion
Walk the cable route for chewed or chafed insulation; check module backsheets for cracks

title: Earth leakage / residual current (GFCI) fault
symptoms: Inverter trips with leakage current high, typically during production or after rain.
causes: Moisture in DC connectors or junction boxes
Poor or missing earthing of module frames and inverter
steps: Check earth pit resistance (target under 5 ohm) and earthing continuity to module frames and inverter
Inspect DC connectors and junction boxes for water ingress
Run an insulation test string by string
If wiring and earthing are healthy and the fault persists, the internal GFCI board may be faulty; escalate to the manufacturer

title: Inverter over-temperature
symptoms: Output derates or shuts down in afternoon; display shows heatsink/internal temperature high.
causes: Inverter installed in direct sunlight or a closed room without ventilation
Clearance around heatsink less than manufacturer minimum
steps: Check installation location: shaded, ventilated, with required clearance (typically 30 cm sides, 50 cm top)
Clean heatsink fins and air vents with power isolated
Check fan operation (see fan fault)
Add a sun shade canopy or relocate inverter if in direct sun

title: PV / DC over-voltage
symptoms: Inverter shows PV voltage too high, especially on cold clear mornings. Risk of permanent damage.
causes: Too many modules in series for the inverter max DC input voltage
Cold-temperature Voc rise not considered in string design
Wrong module datasheet used during design
steps: IMMEDIATELY switch DC isolator OFF to protect the inverter
Measure string open-circuit voltage (Voc) with a DC-rated meter
Recalculate string Voc at minimum site temperature against inverter max input voltage
Re-string with fewer modules per string; do not restart until corrected

title: PV string reverse polarity
symptoms: Inverter shows reverse connection on a string; zero output from that MPPT.
causes: Positive and negative swapped at MC4 or inverter input
steps: Switch DC isolator OFF; do not disconnect MC4 under load
Measure string polarity with a DC meter before reconnecting
Correct the polarity at the string connectors
Inspect inverter input terminals for damage before restart

title: PV low voltage / no PV input
symptoms: Inverter stays in waiting/standby during daylight or one MPPT shows near-zero voltage.
steps: Check DC isolator and DCDB fuses
Measure each string Voc at the DCDB and compare with expected (modules x Voc)
Inspect MC4 connectors for burn marks
Check panels for shading, dust or snow

title: String current mismatch / string abnormal
symptoms: One string produces much less current than others under the same irradiance.
causes: Damaged module or failed bypass diode
steps: Compare string currents in monitoring at midday
Visually inspect the weak string for shading, dirt, bird droppings and cracks
Clean modules
Use IV-curve tracer or clamp meter per module to find failed bypass diodes

title: DC arc fault (AFCI)
symptoms: Inverter locks out with arc fault; may require manual reset. Fire risk.
causes: Loose or poorly crimped MC4 connector
steps: Do NOT repeatedly reset; switch DC isolator OFF
Inspect all DC connectors and terminals for melting, discoloration or burn smell
Replace suspect connectors with same-brand mated pairs crimped with the correct tool
Reset AFCI only after the cause is found

title: DC injection / DCI high
symptoms: Inverter reports DC component in AC output above limit.
steps: Restart the inverter (AC OFF, DC OFF, wait 5 minutes, DC ON, AC ON)
If it recurs, record the fault log and contact manufacturer support; usually requires inverter repair or replacement

title: Grid relay check failure
symptoms: Inverter fails self-test at startup with relay error.
causes: Welded or worn internal AC relay
Large voltage between N and PE
steps: Check neutral wiring at inverter and ACDB
Measure N-PE voltage (should be under ~10 V)
Power-cycle the inverter; if the relay check still fails, the relay or power board needs replacement under warranty

title: DC bus voltage abnormal / unbalanced
symptoms: Inverter trips with internal DC bus voltage error.
steps: Power-cycle the inverter fully
Note whether the fault coincides with cloud edge events or grid disturbances
If persistent, escalate to manufacturer; bus capacitor or power board replacement likely

title: Cooling fan fault
symptoms: Fan alarm; inverter may run with derated output and rising temperature.
causes: Fan blocked by dust, insects or debris
steps: Isolate AC and DC and wait 5 minutes for capacitors to discharge
Remove fan guard and clean debris
Check fan connector seating
Replace the fan with the manufacturer part if it does not spin freely

title: Communication / monitoring fault (WiFi/GPRS logger offline)
symptoms: Monitoring app shows plant offline or no data, but inverter may still be generating.
causes: Home WiFi password changed or router replaced
WiFi signal too weak at inverter location
Data logger stick loose or failed
RS485 cable to energy meter disconnected
steps: Check inverter display to confirm it is still generating
Ask customer whether WiFi password or router changed; reconfigure logger via app/AP mode
Reseat the WiFi/GPRS stick
Check RS485 wiring to the meter (A/B polarity, termination)
Replace data logger if it does not power on

title: Energy meter / CT fault (export limit or zero-export)
symptoms: Export limiting not working, wrong consumption readings, or inverter warns meter lost.
steps: Verify CT arrow direction points toward the grid as per manual
Check CT is on the same phase as the inverter output
Verify meter Modbus address and type in inverter settings
Check RS485 cable continuity

title: Battery low voltage / under-voltage
symptoms: Hybrid inverter cuts backup loads or shows battery low; battery not charging fully.
causes: Deep discharge during long power cuts
Wrong battery type or voltage settings
steps: Check battery voltage at terminals with a multimeter and compare with inverter reading
Tighten battery terminals and check cable lugs for corrosion
Verify battery type, charge voltage and low-voltage cutoff settings
Reduce backup load; allow full charge from grid/PV
For lead-acid check electrolyte level and specific gravity; for lithium check BMS alarms

title: Battery over-voltage
symptoms: Inverter stops charging and reports battery over-voltage.
causes: Charge voltage set too high for battery chemistry
steps: Measure battery voltage at terminals
Correct absorption/float voltage settings to the battery datasheet
Check BMS communication cable (CAN/RS485) for lithium batteries

title: Battery over-temperature
symptoms: Battery charging/discharging stopped due to high battery temperature.
causes: Failing cells with internal resistance rise
steps: Stop operation and let the battery cool; check for swelling, leakage or smell (do not touch swollen batteries)
Move battery to a shaded, ventilated location
Reduce max charge/discharge current setting
Check terminal tightness and lug heating with an IR thermometer
Replace battery if cells are swollen

title: BMS communication fault (lithium battery)
symptoms: Hybrid inverter cannot read the lithium battery; battery treated as missing.
steps: Wake the battery using its power button
Check BMS cable pinout matches inverter manual
Select the correct battery brand/protocol in inverter settings
Update inverter firmware if protocol unsupported

title: Battery reverse polarity / battery not connected
symptoms: Inverter shows no battery or reverse battery connection.
steps: Switch battery breaker OFF before touching cables
Verify polarity with a multimeter
Check battery fuse and breaker
Correct wiring and tighten to specified torque

title: Backup output overload (off-grid / hybrid)
symptoms: Backup output shuts off when a large appliance starts.
causes: Connected backup load exceeds inverter rating
High inrush motor loads (AC, pump, fridge)
steps: List loads on backup circuit and compare with inverter continuous/surge rating
Move heavy loads (AC, geyser, motor pump) off the backup circuit
Check backup wiring for short circuit
Consider soft starter or larger inverter

title: Output short circuit
symptoms: Inverter shuts down immediately with short circuit fault on AC/backup output.
steps: Disconnect all loads and restart
Reconnect loads one at a time to find the faulty circuit
Insulation-test the output wiring
Repair wiring or the faulty appliance

title: Surge protection device (SPD) failure / lightning damage
symptoms: SPD indicator window turned red; inverter may not start after a thunderstorm.
causes: Lightning or switching surge consumed the SPD
steps: Inspect DC and AC SPD indicator windows in DCDB/ACDB
Replace the failed SPD cartridge with matching voltage rating
Check SPD earthing connection and earth pit
Inspect inverter for surge damage before restart

title: Internal memory / control board fault
symptoms: Inverter shows internal/DSP/EEPROM error and will not start.
causes: Communication between master and slave DSP lost
steps: Power-cycle fully (AC OFF, DC OFF, wait 10 minutes)
Update firmware via manufacturer app/USB if available
If persistent, raise a warranty claim with serial number and fault log photo

title: Power module / IGBT / boost fault
symptoms: Inverter trips with hardware overcurrent or power module fault, sometimes with a burning smell.
causes: PV string current exceeding MPPT limit
steps: Switch DC and AC OFF; check for burn smell or discoloration
Verify string short-circuit current is within MPPT input current limit
Do not keep restarting; replace inverter or power board under warranty

title: Low generation without fault code
symptoms: Customer reports fewer units than expected; no active fault code.
causes: New shading from trees or buildings
One string off (blown fuse, loose MC4)
steps: Compare daily kWh with expected (system kW x 4 units/day typical in India)
Clean the panels and check for new shading
Check each MPPT/string voltage and current in monitoring
Check export limit and power factor settings
Review weather history for cloudy days

title: Net meter not recording export / bidirectional meter issue
symptoms: Electricity bill does not show exported units even though the system generates.
causes: Net meter not yet installed or not programmed by DISCOM
Billing system not updated after net metering approval
steps: Check the net meter display for export (kWh-E) register
Confirm net metering agreement and meter installation date with DISCOM
Raise a DISCOM ticket with photos of meter registers
